ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AD \perp BC$ at point $D$. Point $E$ is on $AC$, and $BE$ intersects $AD$ at point $F$. If $BF=AC$ and $DF=DC$, what is the sum of $\angle 1$ and $\angle 2$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AD\perp BC$ at point $D$,\\
it follows that $\angle BDF=\angle ADC=90^\circ$,\\
In $Rt\triangle BDF$ and $Rt\triangle ADC$,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}BF=AC\\ DF=DC\end{array}\right.$,\\
therefore $Rt\triangle BDF \cong Rt\triangle ADC\left(HL\right)$,\\
thus $\angle DBF=\angle 2$, $BD=AD$,\\
hence $\angle DBA=\angle DAB=45^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle 1+\angle 2=\angle 1+\angle DBF=\angle DBA=45^\circ$,\\
therefore the sum of $\angle 1$ and $\angle 2$ is $\boxed{45^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows triangle ABC with A at the top, B at the lower left, and C at the lower right. Segment AD is drawn from A down to BC, meeting BC at D, with a right-angle mark at D. Point E is on side AC, and line BE crosses AD at F. Angle 1 is marked at B between BA and BF. Angle 2 is marked at A between AD and AC. Reasoning: Since AD is perpendicular to BC and F lies on AD while B, D, C lie on BC, both ∠BDF and ∠ADC are right angles. Thus triangles BDF and ADC are right triangles. Given BF = AC and DF = DC, right triangles BDF and ADC are congruent by HL. Therefore corresponding angles give ∠DBF = ∠DAC, and the diagram marks ∠DAC as angle 2. Also corresponding legs give BD = AD. In triangle ABD, ∠BDA = 90° and BD = AD, so triangle ABD is an isosceles right triangle, hence ∠DBA = 45°. From the diagram, ray BF lies inside ∠DBA, so ∠DBA = angle 1 + ∠DBF = angle 1 + angle 2. Therefore angle 1 + angle 2 = 45°.
